newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundi peace talks due to be held in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Burundi peace talks due to be held in Geneva.

text.p: Burundi's Foreign Minister Luc Rukingama said on Thursday the country's warring factions would meet in Geneva next month for a peace conference to prepare talks to end the country's civil war.

"It is not negotiations. It is a preparatory meeting for negotiations. It will be the first time when all groups in Burundi...will meet to discuss peace," Rukingama told a news conference in Brussels, where he was due to meet Belgian and European Union officials.

Rukingama said the conference would be held under the auspices of the United Nations' Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), probably on June 14, although the date remained to be confirmed.

Rukingama said the meeting would be a follow-up to the "discreet phase" of the peace process - talks held in Rome earlier this month with the Hutu rebel National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).

More than 150,000 people have been killed in fighting between Burundi's Tutsi-led army, which seized power last July, and rebels since the killing by soldiers of Burundi's first elected Hutu President in 1993.
Rukingama said a rebel ceasefire was not a condition for the Geneva meeting but that ongoing killings of civilians did pose a barrier to more concrete peace negotiations.
Rukingama said he had learned 50 pupils had been killed overnight in a mission school in the south of the country.
"At the same time the government is trying to discuss with the armed factions about a ceasefire the CNDD continues to kill people which is a big barrier to the peace process," he said.
Rukingama urged international organisations to put pressure on the rebels to respect a ceasefire.

He also called for all sanctions imposed last year when the army seized power to be lifted. African leaders agreed at a meeting in Tanzania last month to ease restrictions on food, medicinal and agricultural products, but Rukingama said the agreement had not been fully applied.
